taster,Seven Silver Spheres in 90 minutes,"A Warden's run plan for [[campaign/seven-silver-spheres
column2: Seven Silver Spheres]] in one 90-minute session, as a prologue to a campaign in [[universe/bith-na-bro
column3: Bith na Bró]]. taster-clock,The clock,"The adventure is set up for Cairn 2e's travel, as its author advises ([[campaign/seven-silver-spheres
column2: the campaign page]] has the details). The party starts at midday on **day 1**, a week before the Autumn Equinox. The temple doors open at dawn on **day 8** and close 24 hours later ([[event/autumn-equinox
column3: The Autumn Equinox]]). A day is three [[rule/procedures-watches
column5: camp]], so a day has two watches of travel.

column1: - **Every leg** (a route between two points), the old road included, is a short forest trail of **3 watches** ([[rule/procedures-travel-duration
column2: Travel Duration]]): a day and a half.

column1: - **Every leg, a d6 to get lost: 1–2** ([[rule/procedures-travel
column3: Path Difficulty]]). Lost, they arrive at a different point from the one they meant: you pick one the route network joins, and it costs them a leg.

column1: - **No rolls on the last leg to the wall** (from the Rising Sun or the Great Oak): the porcelain soldiers keep that ground clear. Through the gatehouse, or along the well passage, takes no watches.

- **Off the trails** (cutting between points no trail joins: the Stones, the Rising Sun and the Oak are 7 to 10 km apart): a short wilderness path, **4 watches**, lost on **1–3**, and a Wilderness Events roll as they leave the trail ([[rule/forest-seeds-exploring-the-wood
column3: the Shadow]]'s ground: lost, they come out where you choose, or where they started. Quicker than two trails round (6 watches), and a gamble.

column1: Every route to the temple is three legs: **9 watches**, from about 13 of travel before the doors open. With nothing lost, the party is at the wall on the evening of day 5, with two days to spare (the table). **One wrong turn they can afford; two, they cannot**, unless they travel at night or skip camp. That is the pressure: let the players count it.
**A condensed ruling for the taster, not the adventure's:** Cairn rolls [[rolltable/procedures-wilderness-events-table
column2: Wilderness Events]] every watch, which is nine rolls a route. In 90 minutes, roll **once a leg**, and narrate camps in a sentence (a Ration each; Fatigue cleared). In the campaign, roll every watch.

taster-after,After the session: making it canon,"Write the outcome down the same day, in up to three layers, because different views see them (the table). Links point down the stack, and neither campaigns nor eras can see each other, so nothing written in this layer or the First Empire's reaches the coming campaign. What is true in every age goes into Bith na Bró itself: an Event after [[event/spheres-scattered
column2: The Seven Spheres are scattered]], say, or where a sphere now lies. How the present remembers it, rumour and gaps included, goes into the Antenexus. The table's detail stays here.

column1: Give each session an entry of its own in this layer: what happened, where it ended, and the threads for next time ([[session/session-1

To write it, append rows to the layer's CSVs, or turn on **Author** in the right view (this one for what happened at the table, Bith na Bró's for what holds in every age, the Antenexus's for the present's version), use **Edit** or **New**, then **Export**, and in the repository run `npm run merge-edits -- cairn-edits-<view>.json` and `npm run check`.
Two things to know before relying on this plan:

- This layer and the First Empire's are still flagged as test layers (""remove when done""), though the First Empire is now Bith na Bró's earlier era, not a stand-in for it. Keep them and the flag should go; remove them and this plan goes with them, and Bith na Bró loses its past.
- The password keeps players from wandering in. It is not security: this layer's CSVs, the plan included, are in a public repository, and its data files are on the published site.",6,taster,,,What

column1: taster-crib,The Warden's crib sheet,"For a first-time Warden, and one who knows Pathfinder: keep this open all session. Its parts are the loop you run all evening, when to roll and what, a fight from start to finish, harm outside a fight, every save this adventure asks for and where, and some lines to have ready.

The one idea under all of it: **the players say what their characters do; you say what happens.** Most of the time nobody rolls. A roll is for a risk the players have chosen to take, and they should know what it is before the dice land ([[rule/overview-and-principles-fiction-first
crib-loop,"The loop, and unlearning Pathfinder","What you do, over and over, all session ([[rule/procedures-wilderness-exploration-cycle
column3: Dungeon]] cycles are this same loop with bookkeeping):

column1: 1. **Describe** where they are, what they can see, hear and smell, and anything dangerous, plainly. Answer every question honestly; there are no perception rolls in Cairn ([[rule/knowledge-and-perception-introduction
2. **Ask ""what do you do?""** If an answer is vague, offer a choice: ""so, the road or the trail?"" ([[rule/overview-and-principles-choice
3. **Resolve it.** Sensible and not risky: it just happens. Risky: say what could go wrong, then call for a save ([[plan/crib-roll
column2: Roll or not]]). Impossible: say no, and offer what they could do instead.

column1: 4. **Consequences:** say what changed, mark off what was used (torches, rations, Fatigue), and go back to 1.
Danger is always telegraphed, the deadlier the more obvious ([[rule/overview-and-principles-danger
column2: Danger]]). If you are about to kill someone and they did not see it coming, stop and describe it first.",1,taster-crib,,,In Pathfinder
column3: In Cairn,"Skill checks against a DC
column4: A save: d20 **at or under** STR, DEX or WIL. No modifiers, no DCs. 1 succeeds, 20 fails.

column1: Perception and Knowledge rolls
column2: None. Tell them what their characters would see or know; the [[rule/overview-and-principles-die-of-fate
column3: Die of Fate]] (d6, 4+ good) if unsure.

column1: Initiative order, creature by creature
column2: Sides: the PCs act, then their enemies. Round 1 only, each PC saves DEX to act.

column1: Attack rolls against AC
column2: None. Attacks hit; roll damage, less armour (at most 3).

column1: HP is health; 0 is dying
column2: HP is luck and dodging, back after a short rest. Wounds are STR loss, and the STR save after.

column1: Classes, levels, feats, XP
column2: None. You are what you carry; you grow from what happens.

column1: Fighting is the main event
column2: Fighting is the last resort, and it is deadly. Talking, sneaking and running are good plans."

column1: crib-roll,"Roll or not, and which","Ask in this order ([[rule/saves-when-to-save
1. **Is there a real risk, with a failure that matters?** If not, no roll: it happens. If the plan is clever, no roll either.
2. **Is it a risk to a character?** Call for a save, and **say the stakes first:** ""make a DEX save; if you fail, you fall into the swamp.""
3. **Is it just chance, with nobody acting** (does she know the old script? is anyone at the camp?)? Roll the [[rule/core-rules-die-of-fate
column2: Die of Fate]]: a d6, 4 or more goes the party's way.

column1: 4. **Is it how a stranger takes them?** Roll [[rolltable/core-rules-reactions-table
column2: Reactions]]: 2d6, from 2 hostile to 12 helpful. Then play the result.

column1: **Saves**: d20, **equal or under** the attribute succeeds; 1 always succeeds, 20 always fails ([[rule/core-rules-saves
column2: Saves]]). Only one roll per risk: if several PCs try something together, **whoever is most at risk rolls** (usually the lowest attribute). Two sides pushing against each other: again, whoever is most at risk rolls; monsters rarely roll at all, except for morale and Critical Damage. A failed save need not be all or nothing: make the outcome fit the effort they put in.",2,taster-crib,,,Save
column4: Lifting, forcing, holding on, swimming against a current, resisting poison, staying up after a wound ([[rule/core-rules-attributes

column2: Acting in round 1, dodging, climbing, sneaking, balancing, running away from a fight

column1: **WIL**
column2: Persuading, deceiving, intimidating, resisting fear or magic, keeping control in the dark, casting a spell in danger"

column1: crib-combat,Running a fight,"**Before it starts.** Telegraph it: the goblins see you, the oak creaks. Give them a choice: talk, back off, sneak round, or fight. If the enemy's mood is unclear, roll [[rolltable/core-rules-reactions-table
column2: Reactions]] first. If they still fight:

column1: 1. **Round 1: every PC makes a DEX save to act.** Fail: they lose their turn this round ([[rule/core-rules-rounds
column2: Rounds]]). If the PCs set the ambush, waive it.

column1: 2. **The PCs declare, then resolve.** All the PCs say what they do, then roll; their results land together. Each may move about 40ft and take one action: attack, cast a spell, move again, or something else sensible ([[rule/core-rules-actions
column2: Actions]]). Anything risky beyond attacking (a shove off the bridge) is a save.

column1: 3. **Damage.** Attacks hit: roll the weapon's die, take off the target's armour, take the rest off HP ([[rule/core-rules-attacking-damage
column2: Attacking & Damage]]). Several attackers on one target: roll them all, **keep the single highest**. Fighting from weakness (cover, bound, a long shot) is _impaired_: d4. From advantage (a helpless foe, a daring move) it is _enhanced_: d12. _Blast_ hits everyone in the area, a roll for each ([[rule/core-rules-attack-modifiers

column1: 4. **The enemies' turn**, the same way. Then a new round: the PCs go first, no DEX saves now.
**When damage lands on a PC:**
- **HP left:** nothing worse; they were lucky.
- **HP to exactly 0:** a Scar. Look up the HP lost in that attack on [[rolltable/core-rules-scars-table-table

- **Past 0:** the rest comes off **STR**, and they **save STR at the new score** straight away. Pass: still fighting. Fail: **Critical Damage**. A PC can only crawl, and dies within the hour unless someone tends them (bandages stabilise). Some monsters do worse on a failed save ([[rule/core-rules-critical-damage
**When damage lands on a monster:** the same, but a failed Critical Damage save means it is dead.
**Morale.** Enemies save **WIL** when they lose their first, and again when they are down to half; a lone foe saves at 0 HP. Fail: they flee or give up ([[rule/core-rules-morale
